impact_pathways.impact_narrative: The project measures the same agricultural pressure gradient across farmland, freshwater ecotones and coastal waters. Three campaigns run under one protocol in WP4 and deliver comparable observation datasets (D4.1-D4.4). The classification and trend models in WP6 extend that evidence to European coverage (D6.2, D6.3). Each trend prediction carries the uncertainty the case benchmarks measured. Knowledge of status, trends and drivers improves because one measurement culture now spans three realms.
impact_pathways.tier2b_source_ref: Destination 'Biodiversity and ecosystem services' — Expected impact (WP Part 9, p.47)

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: WP3 releases the joint protocols, the crosswalk package and the provenance-tracked pipeline under FAIR terms (D3.1-D3.4). WP6 releases the classification models and their benchmarks (D6.2, D6.3). All are published to the open science cloud and the common data spaces. A group outside the consortium can apply them without asking the consortium for anything. The methods are available; the project measures reuse rather than promising it.
impact_pathways.tier2b_source_ref: Destination 'Biodiversity and ecosystem services' — Expected impact (WP Part 9, p.47)

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: The three cases share one pressure and one measurement protocol. The project reports how the same agricultural load registers in the terrestrial, freshwater and marine realms (D4.1-D4.4). A single-realm study cannot ask that question. The molecular layer in WP5 joins genomic observation to the in-situ and remote-sensing record (D5.1-D5.3). Understanding of the crisis improves because the pathway from land to coast becomes observable.
impact_pathways.tier2b_source_ref: Destination 'Biodiversity and ecosystem services' — Expected impact (WP Part 9, p.47)

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: The reporting-needs assessment in WP7 runs before the outputs are designed (D7.1). A competent authority can then use them without rework. The crosswalks in WP3 make a habitat label resolvable against the reporting classifications. Stakeholder work runs across the whole project, not as a closing phase (D7.4). The valuation clause of this impact is only partly addressed, and the project claims no valuation it does not run.
impact_pathways.tier2b_source_ref: Destination 'Biodiversity and ecosystem services' — Expected impact (WP Part 9, pp.47-48)
impact_pathways.note: The valuation clause within EI-04 is marked Unresolved in Tier 3 impacts.json: no partner carries environmental economics, so the project improves the evidence a valuation rests on but runs none.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: Indicators derived from the observation chain reach farm-management tools through an existing multi-country user network (D7.2, D7.3). Practitioners are asked whether they can act on them. The protocol transfer in WP7 tests whether a second production context can run the same measurement. The uptake channel is a capability of one partner whose participation is Assumed. If that partner does not join, this pathway loses its route to practitioners.
impact_pathways.tier2b_source_ref: Destination 'Biodiversity and ecosystem services' — Expected impact (WP Part 9, p.48)

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: Every habitat label the project publishes carries a crosswalk to the European classification and to a global ecosystem typology (D3.2). Project occurrence records are published to the global data facilities the topic names (D3.4). WP3 builds the crosswalks and takes the harmonisation decisions to the standards bodies. The evidence becomes countable in an international assessment.
impact_pathways.tier2b_source_ref: Destination 'Biodiversity and ecosystem services' — Expected impact (WP Part 9, p.48)

Every released label carries a crosswalk to the European classification and to a global ecosystem typology so the evidence is countable in an international assessment.

exploitation_plan.ipr_strategy: Results are released as open methods, data and models under FAIR and open licences, because the exploitation route the project claims is uptake and reuse, not proprietary protection. Tier 3 carries no explicit IPR data, so no protection measure is asserted beyond open licensing and non-proprietary contributions to the standards bodies. The valuation clause within the fourth destination impact is not exploited: no partner carries environmental economics, and the project improves the evidence a valuation rests on rather than running one.

sustainability_mechanism.description: Results persist because the methods, data and models are released FAIR to the European Open Science Cloud, the common data spaces and the global data facilities, where they remain available and reusable after the project without any consortium involvement. Every project habitat label resolves through the crosswalk package to the maintained European classification and to a global ecosystem typology, and the harmonisation decisions are taken to the standards bodies that maintain those classifications. Adoption by those bodies embeds the results in infrastructures that outlive the four-year project. The practitioner route to farm-management tools runs through an existing multi-country user network that continues after project end, though it depends on one partner whose participation is Assumed.
responsible_partners: WP3 lead (open-science releases, crosswalks and standards submissions)
WP6 lead (models, benchmarks and training resource)
